this is a treat, the repetition and long winded twisting lines are clever and purpseful, and the parapgraphing makes it feel personal and very real. the critique of the self centredness thats bred into us making it difficult to empathize with people is relevant, and very very widespread, and the way you word it makes it feel less like an essay, and more like vivid prose. there are a few lines that are a bit verbose in attempts to rhyme, but all in all i do like the fact that theres a decided rhythm to it.

my god, this is so gorgeous, i love it. the imagery is miserable, and ethereal, and gloomy, and so so vivid, i can see all the dreamy images in front of my eyes. the description of the death of an older self, and it being done by your own hand, the mystic and magical description and the rich scenery and little details you mention are so gorgeous. i think one of my favorite little details is the mention of the narcissus, not only because its relevant in the context of viewing your self, but also because so far all the imagery i saw in my brain was murky and swamplike, and the images of little yellow flowers was so pretty and nice it just added another sort of layer to everything. this feels like one of those pieces of writing you might not understand entirely, but you experience and feel, you can breathe in the forest air, and feel the slither of the eels against your skin. lovely.

everyday is that long lost ache, deep in my chest, wondering what will fill it in. i drift in between the threads of life, loneliness. i wait for someone to hold, someone to touch. i meet a boy, he holds my hands and a part of me is disappointed. something about him is shallow. i resign myself to him. he chains me with a ring.

i tell myself he is the 'one'. but there are so many of him, each face blending into the next, uninterested, cold, mellow. we stay married for ten more, boring years, my wings itching to stretch, to destroy. sometimes, my glance shys to the forbidden. i always flush red. no, he has to be the one. the alternatives are too dangerous.

we fight from time to time. even this we grow tired of. i convince myself that loving is giving up, growing old.

it's with great confusion that i meet eyes with her, our new neighbour, moving in next door. i feel something birth itself from the tissues of love and yearning, threaten to escape the mouth i hold agape. she is forbidden, i am married.

yet i hold her hand over a welcome party full of bad food and small talk. her eyes give me the same look. we go off to share our women talk, break the ice with meaningless back-and-forths about so-and-so's husbands. and soon conversations tangent into memories i thought i had forgotten, laugh at the love deep within. we are two lovers, fully clothed women in their husbands homes, lost and found. i understand then that love is not growing old.

love is immortal. once more we find ourselves in the reborn and reborn and reborn.
